Subject: Post-call: Performance & network qualification for Private/VPC deployment (Acme)

Thanks for joining the call today — good conversation. Short recap and agreed next steps below so we have alignment on performance targets and what we need from your side to qualify a Private/VPC deployment.

Key SLOs (as discussed)
- Latency: target p50 <= 100ms, p95 <= 300ms for 1k token responses (streaming enabled).
- Throughput/concurrency: baseline 500 QPS sustained, burst up to 1.5k QPS; concurrency per model ~80 concurrent streams.
- Streaming: chunked responses (server-sent events); we need end-to-end first-byte times <120ms on average to keep UX smooth.

Network qualification items (what we need from Acme)
1) Network diagram and egress path (public internet vs. VPC peering/direct interconnect).
2) VPN/peering details: IP ranges, ASN, BGP session info if peering, and any proxy/load‑balancer in front of your hosts.
3) Typical internal latency numbers (your app -> gateway -> peered VPC) and any NAT/egress gateways.
4) Expected packet MTU and whether you support jumbo frames.

Notes/actions
- Jordan will validate with infra (Dev Patel) whether peering vs. VPN meets the p95 budget.
- Acme to send network diagram and sample traceroutes/iperf results by EOD 2028-05-16.
- We'll provide a small test checklist and traffic profile (attached: redwood-vpc-requirements.pdf).

Attachments: redwood-vpc-requirements.pdf (requirements/spec), test checklist will follow.

Next meeting: propose Wed 2028-05-17 09:00 PT for network ops deep-dive — please confirm.

Thanks,

Thanks for the forward — reviewed the diagram and notes. High-level assessment below.

1) Peering vs. VPN
- Direct VPC peering or a cloud interconnect (Direct Connect / Cloud Interconnect) is strongly preferred for sub-10ms internal latency and predictable jitter.
- IPSec VPN will work for initial testing, but expect additional overhead (~20–40ms) and possible MTU/path-MTU issues that can push p95 above our target, especially for larger payloads/streamed chunks.

2) Transit VPC / NAT concerns
- NAT/egress gateways add both latency and variability; if Acme routes traffic through a transit VPC for vendor egress, we should measure end‑to‑end and treat the transit path as a potential source of 50–120ms extra p95 depending on topology.

3) Recommended network configurations
- Prefer: direct peering + BGP for vendor subnets + advertised /32s for Redwoods' endpoints.
- If direct peering not possible: a dedicated IPSec link with static routes and jumbo frames enabled; avoid hairpinning through transit NAT where possible.
- TCP tuning: enable keepalives (30s), increase TCP window (autoscaling offload is fine), and enable TLS session resumption to avoid handshake overhead on short-lived connections.

4) Throughput & concurrency notes
- For 500 QPS sustained with 80 concurrency: recommend enabling batching on the server side to reduce per-request overhead; this will lower the network packet rate.
- Consider caching static prefixes or using prefix/KV cache if many requests share prompts — reduces egress and latency.

5) Test plan (attached network_test_checklist.xlsx) — quick tests to run before our Wed call:
- Traceroute from Acme app to candidate Redwoods IPs (3 repeats)
- Iperf3 tests (TCP/UDP) for 30s windows at expected concurrency levels
- Sample payload test using 1k token stream to measure first-byte & last-byte times
- Record MTU and any intermediate firewall/proxy that may rewrite headers

Next steps
- John / Acme: please run the checklist and share results prior to Wed 09:00 PT. If results show VPN >150ms p95, we should schedule a follow-up to scope a dedicated interconnect.
- I'll prepare a short network ops slide (1 page) to walk through during the Wed call.

Attachments: network_test_checklist.xlsx

Happy to jump on the call with NetOps.
